record.tranche_reason: The study derives a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction and applies direction ablation across residual streams, then tests weight orthogonalization on a new model. It reports qualitative harmful-prompt outcomes rather than a standardized refusal rate.
record.gate_note: The study reports qualitative outcomes for four harmful test prompts and a text-described benchmark performance drop after weight editing. Direction rankings and the four-prompt screen are used to choose the direction/layer, so those selection values are not separate results. The article also describes adding the direction to induce refusal, but does not perform that intervention.
record.test_reason: A tutorial blog post. It computes a harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction on Daredevil-8B, ablates it at inference time and through weight orthogonalization, and reports the effect on refusal and on benchmarks. The evidence is qualitative (four prompts, no refusal rate) and partly circular, because the direction was chosen on the same four prompts used to show success.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The author concludes that abliteration uncensors Daredevil-8B without retraining but degrades performance. DPO healing recovers most of it, giving a 'fully uncensored' high-quality model. The author also notes that this shows safety fine-tuning is fragile.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless residual activation means and direction projection ablation, but ranks directions and manually selects a candidate using four harmful prompts, then demonstrates weight orthogonalization. It does not test adding the direction or use a quantified refusal-rate evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The implementation selects resid_pre directions, ranks candidates, and manually chooses candidate #9 after screening 20 directions on four harmful prompts. No systematic outcome comparison across candidates or residual stream choices is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: DPO fine-tuning on orpo-dpo-mix-40k recovers most of the benchmark loss from abliteration, except on GSM8K.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc preference training can repair capability losses caused by refusal-direction weight edits.

record.problems: The harmful-prompt outcome is qualitative and uses only four test instructions. No refusal-rate figures or uncertainty estimates are reported. Benchmark results appear as images without values in the supplied text, and the article notes performance loss after abliteration.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported benchmark values could be extracted from the benchmark images; the text gives only aggregate descriptions. Direction-ranking values and candidate-screen outputs were used to select the direction and are not treated as outcome rows.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal (described as background only), refusal on harmless prompts, and quantified refusal rates.
Refusal rates on a held-out harmful set, and models beyond Daredevil-8B.

record.verdict_notes: This is a non-peer-reviewed tutorial. The direction is selected by inspecting outputs on the same 4 prompts used to demonstrate success, and there are no quantified refusal metrics. Benchmark numbers are in images only. The ability to induce refusal by adding the direction is cited from Arditi et al., not tested here.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction, refusal on harmless prompts, or whether abilities are largely preserved without subsequent DPO training.
Tests weight orthogonalization on one model with qualitative harmful-prompt outputs; does not quantify refusal rates or test other released models.
No jailbreak suppression or robustness training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of one direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages.

relation.reason: Its own ablation and weight-edit results on Daredevil-8B bear on V1 and V2, though they are qualitative.

tranche.reason: Same difference-in-means direction, directional ablation and weight orthogonalization as Arditi et al. Refusal is judged by substring filter plus reading, and capability by Open LLM Leaderboard tasks. The method is close but the measure is much cruder: 4 prompts, selection on the test prompts.

source_check.notes: The pack gave no [lN] ids, so label_ids l1-l4 follow the order the verdicts are listed. Header metadata is off: the title is 'Uncensor any LLM with abliteration' ('Fine-tuning without retraining' is the subtitle), and it is dated Jun 12, 2024. Only resid_pre directions are ranked (by abs(mean) of the unit vector), and candidates are pre-filtered on 'I cannot'/'I can't' before manual selection on the 4 test prompts, so the success claim is circular. There is no random-direction control.

statements.correction: Labonne: Daredevil-8B is a DARE TIES mega-merge, loaded under the name Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Directions: harmful-minus-harmless mean at the last token over 256 prompts each, ranked by abs(mean). The top 20 were ablated at inference on 4 harmful test prompts (greedy, 64 tokens), filtered on 'I cannot'/'I can't', then judged by reading. Candidate 9 'provide[d] uncensored answer for the four instructions'. W_E, attention W_O and MLP W_out were orthogonalized against candidate 9 and pushed as Daredevil-8B-abliterated. The text says this 'successfully uncensored it' with no outputs or refusal rate. The 4 prompts were also used for selection. Header: controls n, capability y, uncertainty n, code y (Colab). The post says it 'introduced the concept', but the 'abliterated' name comes from FailSpy's earlier work.
statements.problem: Numbers for this study (4 prompts, candidate 9, 64 tokens, greedy) are right. Problems: (1) The 'why' says the header has controls y, but the header has controls=n and the text has no control beyond unablated baseline generations, which it does not show. (2) 'Uncensored on 4 test prompts' is stated for the inference-time candidate #9. The weight-edited release is only called 'successfully uncensored', and no outputs are shown. (3) The text does not say 'instruct-based'. (4) The term predates the post: FailSpy's abliterator library and 'abliterated' models came first.
